songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World
It's All Over Now Baby Blue

supporting_acts: Jack Casady, Jorma Kaukonen, and Joey Covington

ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star>St Stephen>The Eleven, stellar Dire Wolf & Casey Jones
ai_show_review.blurb: The set shines with a soaring Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite and an inspired Dire Wolf featuring Bob’s lead vocals. A high‑energy rendition of Casey Jones and an unexpected turn into Green Green Grass Of Home round out a memorable night.
ai_show_review.review: June 27 1969 finds the Dead in Santa Rosa delivering one of their most adventurous early shows. After a relaxed country‑tinged opening with Slewfoot* and Mama Tried, the band rockets into a blistering second half highlighted by a luminous Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven journey that showcases Jerry’s pedal‑steel flavor and Phil’s deep Lovelight jam beneath. Bob Weir steps to the mic on Dire Wolf, giving the song a confident, almost gospel feel, while the unexpected Green Green Grass Of Home adds a whimsical twist before closing with a heartfelt Baby Blue. Throughout, the rhythm section tightens after an initially loose drum feel, evolving into fluid double‑drum interplay that drives the high‑energy vibe of the night.

best_recording.reason: Highest‑quality soundboard tape with clear mix, captures the full dynamic range of the performance

key_highlights: Luminous Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite with soaring guitar and deep bass
Bob’s standout lead vocal on Dire Wolf adds a country‑gospel texture
Energetic early version of Casey Jones that drives the set forward
Surprising, upbeat turn to Green Green Grass Of Home before the gentle Baby Blue encore
song_highlights: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

band_performance.Jerry: Pedal‑steel work on Slewfoot*, Dire Wolf and Green Grass adds country flavor; his lead guitar shines throughout, especially in the Dark Star suite.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid bass foundation with a deep Lovelight jam during Dark Star, anchoring the extended improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Delivers confident lead vocals on Dire Wolf, giving the song a standout presence; also contributes rhythm guitar throughout.
band_performance.Brent: Tom Constanten's organ adds drippy texture, notably on Baby Blue, enriching the gospel‑like feel of the encore.
band_performance.Mickey: After an initially loose feel, Mickey locks in with Bill for fluid double‑drum work that propels the high‑energy second half.
band_performance.Billy: Provides steady drive early on and later blends seamlessly into the dual‑drum groove, keeping the set tight.
